AZ-2026-SB1713.aiSummary: Arizona would change how AHCCCS, the state health care program, chooses and reviews managed care contractors. It would set a new process that uses a published performance score, a four-year review period, and rules for who can get or keep contracts, starting October 1, 2026. The law also sets limits on enrollment levels for contractors and applies to AHCCCS, long-term care, and children’s health insurance programs.

AZ-2026-SB1671.aiSummary: The law continues the state gaming department, the racing commission, and the boxing and mixed martial arts commission, and sets new end dates for them in 2032. It also requires leaders and employees in these agencies to file conflict-of-interest forms when hired or appointed and update them each year if anything changes. The gaming department must create a public complaint process and tracking system, file yearly complaint reports, and review older event wagering audits to check fee payments and fix any overpayments or underpayments.

AZ-2026-SB1160.aiSummary: The law limits drone use near ticketed entertainment events like concerts, sports, and shows held in gated areas. It makes it a crime to fly a drone within 5,280 feet of or above such an event unless the flyer has permission or fits a listed exception, like certain workers or flying over their own property for noncommercial use. It also keeps cities and counties from making their own rules on drone ownership or use in most cases.

AZ-2026-HB2174.aiSummary: This law updates Arizona insurance rules by replacing the term "advisory organization" with "modeling and data organization" in several places. It lets these groups gather and share insurance data and lets the insurance director review and examine them under the same kinds of rules. It also keeps the current rules for rate making, data sharing, and penalties for late reports.

AZ-2026-SB1286.aiSummary: The bill lets a veterinarian form a client-patient relationship through electronic means, except for animals used in commercial food production. It requires client consent, gives clients the vet’s contact and license info, and says the vet must explain limits on care by video or other electronic visits. It also lets vets prescribe drugs after an electronic exam, with limits on renewals and no controlled substances unless the vet has done an in-person exam or timely on-site visits. The bill passed and was signed by the Governor.

AZ-2026-SB1013.aiSummary: The bill would have barred the state and local governments from using hiring rules that require jobs to be filled on anything other than merit, meaning a person's skills, experience, and ability. It would also have limited efforts to shape the makeup of employees by race, ethnicity, sex, or national origin, except as needed to follow anti-discrimination laws. It would have allowed lawsuits for violations and was passed before being vetoed by the governor.

versions.label: HOUSE - Floor Amend to Bill - Weninger - passed

documents.label: House COW 03/04 - Floor Amend to Bill - Weninger

AZ-2026-HB4043.aiSummary: Beginning August 1, 2026, public high schools that sponsor sports would have to provide an automated external defibrillator, or AED, at each campus and at school sports events, and keep it in a marked, easy-to-reach place. Beginning August 1, 2027, each school district and charter school would have to have at least one staff member at each campus during regular hours trained in CPR and first aid, and also trained to use an AED if one is on campus. Schools could accept gifts and donations to help buy and maintain AEDs. The bill was signed by the governor.

AZ-2026-HB2979.aiSummary: The bill changes Arizona rules for credit unions. It sets time limits for the state deputy director to respond to requests about bylaw changes, name changes, and changes to a main office or branch, and it lets credit unions ask to use powers tied to out-of-state credit unions by filing a request. It also updates rules on credit committee votes, share accounts, and several other credit union powers.

AZ-2026-HB2482.aiSummary: The bill would change rules for Arizona school building renewal grants and how school districts apply for them. It would add more reporting, inspection, and project review steps, and it would set a $1,000,000 cap on an individual job order for construction work paid with building renewal grant money. AZ-2026-HB2321.aiSummary: The law requires the Department of Child Safety to place a credit freeze on a child’s credit record within 30 days after the child is found dependent and placed in the department’s care. The freeze stays in place until the child turns 16, when the child can choose to keep it or remove it, and the department must notify the parent or guardian when the freeze is placed or remains in place. It also updates state rules for credit reporting agencies on how to place or remove these freezes, and says they may not charge a fee for doing so.

AZ-2026-HB2265.aiSummary: Arizona changed several court fee rules and fee limits for criminal and civil cases. It bars courts from charging many fees or reimbursements to indigent people, juveniles, and criminal defendants for public defense, appeals, and some transcripts, while also changing how some court fees and jury fees are collected and used.
